title: Merge Two Sorted Arrays
statement:
Merge two ascending arrays into one ascending array.

## Your function

```
void merge_sorted(const int *a, int count_a,
                  const int *b, int count_b,
                  int *out);
```

Both inputs are already sorted ascending. Write all `count_a + count_b` values
into `out`, in ascending order. The caller has made `out` big enough.

## Watch out

- One walk through each array is enough: compare the two front elements, take
  the smaller, advance that one. Concatenating and then sorting works and
  throws away everything the inputs already told you.
- When one array runs out, the rest of the other one is copied across
  unchanged. Two of the three loops you write do nothing but that.
- Either array may be empty, and both may be. An empty array's pointer may be
  `NULL`, so the count has to be checked before the pointer is read.
- Values may repeat, both within an array and across the two.

tests.name: both empty
tests.description: Nothing to merge. Both pointers may be NULL.

tests.name: first empty
tests.description: The whole of the second array is copied across.

tests.name: one entirely before the other
tests.description: The first array empties before the second is touched.
